items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: So, that's why I told him, if he gets rid of John, he has to get rid of me.

ctx.x: ...Casa? Ask him about the Casa. What about Casa?

Casa? Casa? You're here talking in there. We used to play the Casa a lot of times too, you know. And I don't know but... ...if he had to come to my house that day, he might have been living today. When he first come back from California, he come to see me. And he say, what you doing, Dad? I said, nothing man, time. Kind of... ...dove down there. He says, uh... ...well, why don't you... ...we and you get together and get up a little four or five piece bag? I said, that's what I've been waiting for. I said, I think…
Ask him why he's got Zeb and Ernest Kelly together. Zeb was a fine fella. You see what?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: John Kazman. Then I worked with that team at the doghouse for about three years and a half.

ctx.x: Ask him who he worked with in that district. What? Ask him who he worked with in the district. What band?
So who did you work with in the district? What bands? John Kazman. Then I worked with that team at the doghouse for about three years and a half.
Yeah, but I mean around the Tuxedo and the 25.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: Then I was with, uh, called it the John Casman band at that time.

ctx.x: Why not? Ask me if you knew shots.

Did you know shots? Shots, huh, Ruby? I was playing with him. Shots played with us in the full place. I was playing with him. Shots was another liquor-head, too. He was a good corner player, but he was a liquor-head. Shots drank so much whiskey to the kids. He played with us until he got kind of sick. And he wasn't sick so long before he died. He was a good corner player, Shots. Which band was that? Whose band? Well, we was a make-up band, I thought. We didn't have no special name. Then I was with, uh, called it…
